36.old: Maple Ridge is in School District 42 (SD42). Names, grades and addresses from the Province’s Maple Ridge school list and SD42. Checked against the official pages on October 17, 2026.
36.new: Cottonwood falls under School District 42 (SD42), as does the rest of Maple Ridge. Names, grades and addresses are from SD42 and the Province’s Maple Ridge school list, verified using the official pages on October 17, 2026.

62.old: Metro Vancouver lists trails for walking, cycling and horseback riding. Canyon Trail runs from the fish hatchery to Cliff Falls, 1.2 km one way with some challenging hills. The flat Riverfront Trails are 3 km one way
62.new: Metro Vancouver’s trail list covers walking, cycling and horseback riding. Canyon Trail starts at the fish hatchery and ends at Cliff Falls, 1.2 km one way, and it has some challenging hills. The Riverfront Trails are flat, at 3 km one way.

87.old: Lot size (MLS sales data, not an official source): the median lot size of detached houses sold between July 1 and October 8, 2026 was 5,995 sq ft, based on 14 sales with a recorded lot size.
87.new: For detached houses that sold from July 1 through October 8, 2026, MLS sales data (not an official source) gives a median lot size of 5,995 sq ft. That rests on 14 sales, each with a recorded lot size.

107.old: The City mails its Be Flood Ready guide to properties near the Fraser River floodplain. The guide includes a map of the Fraser River floodplain and an overview of the City’s flood response plan.
107.new: The Be Flood Ready guide is mailed out by the City to properties near the Fraser River floodplain. It has a Fraser River floodplain map plus an outline of the City’s plan for responding to floods.

108.old: The City says a floodplain map shows the area expected to flood on average once every 200 years, and it publishes floodplain maps for the Fraser and Alouette rivers.
108.new: Floodplain maps for the Fraser and Alouette rivers are published by the City, which says that a floodplain map marks the area that is expected to flood, on average, once in every 200 years.

109.old: The City says it manages flood risk case by case, and that a proposed Floodplain Management Bylaw would set clearer rules, including minimum building elevations.
109.new: Maple Ridge says flood risk gets dealt with one case at a time, and a Floodplain Management Bylaw it has proposed would spell out clearer rules, minimum building elevations among them.

113.old: TransLink’s Langley–Haney Place Bus Rapid Transit line would run 22 km with 13 stations and service every 10 minutes at peak. TransLink says it is in detailed planning with preliminary funding through the 2025 Investment Plan, and that more funding is needed to deliver it.
113.new: At peak times, the Langley–Haney Place Bus Rapid Transit line TransLink has planned would run every 10 minutes along 22 km and 13 stations. TransLink reports detailed planning is under way, and that the 2025 Investment Plan gave preliminary funding but more is required to deliver it.

120.old: The timetable dates and TransLink’s fall 2026 service changes are noted in the transit card and the get-around answer, so check the current schedule.
120.new: Check the current schedule, since the transit card and the get-around answer both note TransLink’s fall 2026 service changes and the timetable dates.

151.old: Kanaka Creek Regional Park is 400 hectares along 12 kilometres of Kanaka Creek, with Cliff Falls as the focal point.
151.new: Cliff Falls is the focal point of Kanaka Creek Regional Park, which spans 12 kilometres of Kanaka Creek and covers 400 hectares.

153.old: The Maple Ridge Public Library is at 130 – 22470 Dewdney Trunk Road, and it is the only Fraser Valley Regional Library branch in Maple Ridge.
153.new: Maple Ridge has just one Fraser Valley Regional Library branch, the Maple Ridge Public Library at 130 – 22470 Dewdney Trunk Road.
